title: Second-ideal quotient systems are annihilated by the thickening ideal
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I and K quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, M a coherent I-adic formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and e ≥ 0. Every term M_n/K^(e+1)M_n, using the recursive module quotient of that definition, is annihilated by the kernel ideal of the closed immersion V(K^(e+1)) → X. This is scheme-theoretic annihilation, including nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 088A, construction of G_e and their adjacent quotient maps

proof.text: At each level the term is the cokernel quotient by the recursive K-power product. The existing private idealModuleProduct_quotient_zero theorem in CoherentFormalModule proves annihilation by this recursive power.

Rewrite the closed-immersion kernel with ker_subschemeι. Reuse power_inclusion_iso and product_inclusion_iso from ThickeningSystemPushforwardAdic (import all): the former identifies the positive recursive power inclusion with (K^(e+1)).toModulesι, and the latter identifies their multiplication images on the quotient. Transfer the zero-object property across that isomorphism. These helpers are already proved using the affine-section ideal-power formula, not assumed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 088A, construction of G_e; second reading by W4 closes the Lean proof using existing recursive-power/product isomorphisms and cokernel annihilation.
